purpose: machine-usable expert-system knowledge base for finding, evaluating, and applying authoritative methods of negotiation, persuasion, and conflict resolution as concrete, evaluable work units within a knowledge-searcher meta-KB
assumptions: subdomain of professional communication and speaking; scope is negotiation, persuasion/influence, and conflict resolution
nodes are concrete negotiation/influence work units, methods, or decision areas
no observed dataset supplied; all numeric values are heuristic priors
key references: Fisher/Ury/Patton Getting to Yes; Cialdini Influence; Stone/Patton/Heen Difficult Conversations
ethics red lines forbid deception and coercion regardless of effectiveness
exclusions: legal contract drafting and litigation procedure
sales funnel mechanics and pricing strategy as such
cross-cultural protocol specifics beyond general adaptation
public speaking delivery and slide design

competency_questions.question: Given a problem or relationship, how should the negotiation be framed (parties, issues, interests, horizon, success criteria)?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: NEGOTIATION_FRAMING maps the problem to a bounded deal frame

competency_questions.question: How are each side's underlying interests separated from stated positions and mapped to tradeable dimensions?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: INTEREST_MAPPING traces every position to an interest

competency_questions.question: How are BATNAs, reservation values, and the ZOPA determined and used to set the walk-away point?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BATNA_ANALYSIS and ZOPA_RESERVATION yield walk-away and deal zone

competency_questions.question: When should value be created (integrative) versus claimed (distributive), and how is the tension managed?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: VALUE_CREATION and VALUE_CLAIMING with their conflict axis resolve the negotiator's dilemma

competency_questions.question: Which tactics (anchoring, concessions, framing) apply and how are they sequenced and bounded?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ANCHORING_OFFERS, CONCESSION_STRATEGY, FRAMING_TACTICS are sequenced from the ZOPA

competency_questions.question: How is the authority and evidence strength of a negotiation or persuasion source or tactic graded?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SOURCE_AUTHORITY_EVAL grades each principle by evidence strength

competency_questions.question: Which persuasion principle (reciprocity, social proof, authority, scarcity, commitment, liking) applies, and how is it used ethically and detected when used against you?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: the six principle nodes specify ethical use and detection

competency_questions.question: How are listening, difficult conversations, and de-escalation used to keep emotional, high-stakes talks productive?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ACTIVE_LISTENING, DIFFICULT_CONVERSATIONS, DEESCALATION cover the conflict-resolution skills

competency_questions.question: When and how is a neutral third-party mediation process designed and run?
Where is the line between ethical persuasion and manipulation, and how is the agreement closed honestly and durably?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ETHICS_INFLUENCE_GUARDRAILS and AGREEMENT_CLOSURE set red lines and durable terms

competency_questions.question: In what order should negotiation work units be executed to minimize rework, and which must not be finalized before others?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: priority_order and anti_rework_rules give the rework-minimizing sequence

competency_questions.question: How are high-risk or irreversible moves (entry-equivalent commitments, advantage claims) escalated for human review before lock?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: validation_protocol human-review thresholds gate high-risk nodes

glossary.definition: interests are the underlying needs/constraints; positions are the stated demands that purport to satisfy them
best alternative to a negotiated agreement: the course of action if no deal is reached
the worst deal terms a side will accept, derived from its BATNA
zone of possible agreement: the overlap between the two sides' reservation values
creating joint value by trading across differently-valued issues
claiming a share of a fixed surplus
the first or reference number that biases the perceived bargaining range
evidence-based levers of persuasion: reciprocity, social proof, authority, scarcity, commitment, liking
the what-happened, feelings, and identity layers of a difficult conversation
manipulation uses deception or coercion; persuasion uses honest, voluntary influence

evidence_label_policy.note: No observed/experimental inputs supplied; only heuristic labels are eligible.

source_registry.description: Heuristic priors from established negotiation and influence literature (Fisher, Ury & Patton 'Getting to Yes'; Ury 'Getting Past No'; Cialdini 'Influence'; Stone, Patton & Heen 'Difficult Conversations'; Lax & Sebenius '3-D Negotiation'; Fisher & Shapiro 'Beyond Reason') and standard practice; no measured dataset supplied.
grounding_limits: all numeric values are heuristic priors, not measurements
no observed or experimentally_validated labels are eligible

normalization_definitions.rounding: round computed scores to 2 decimals; tolerance 0.02

nodes.definition: Frame the negotiation as a bounded problem: parties, issues, interests at stake, constraints, time horizon, and what a good outcome means before tactics.
contradictors: tactician who opens before scoping the deal

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the mandate, parties, or what counts as a good outcome changes

pros.claim: a clear frame keeps every later tactic anchored to the real decision
pros.example: scope a salary talk as 'comp + role + start date', not just 'more money')

cons.claim: a wrong frame makes strong tactics solve the wrong problem
cons.example: haggling price when the real issue is delivery risk

acceptance_tests: frame states parties, issues, horizon, and success criteria
decision authority of each side named

nodes.definition: Elicit and map underlying interests, needs, and constraints of all sides, separating them from stated positions to expose tradeable and shared interests.
contradictors: positional bargainer who never asks 'why'

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a party reveals a new interest or a stated position shifts

pros.claim: separating interests from positions reveals trades that positions hide
pros.example: 'I need it by Friday' (interest) vs 'I won't pay over X' (position))

cons.claim: inferred interests can be wrong and bias the whole plan
cons.example: assuming the other side wants price when they want security

acceptance_tests: each position traced to an underlying interest
shared and opposed interests separated

nodes.definition: Determine and improve each side's best alternative to a negotiated agreement so the walk-away point is grounded in real options, not bluff.
contradictors: negotiator who enters with no alternative

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when an outside option appears, expires, or the counterpart's alternatives change

pros.claim: a strong, real BATNA is the single largest source of leverage
pros.example: having a second job offer sets your true walk-away)

cons.claim: overestimating your BATNA leads to walking away from good deals
cons.example: treating a vague 'maybe' offer as a firm alternative

acceptance_tests: own BATNA is a concrete, available option
walk-away trigger defined before talks

nodes.definition: Convert BATNAs into reservation values and locate the zone of possible agreement, or conclude no deal zone exists.
contradictors: negotiator who sets a target with no reservation value

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when either side's BATNA or reservation value is revised

pros.claim: a mapped ZOPA tells you whether a deal is even possible and where to aim
pros.example: if their max is below your min, stop and improve BATNA)

cons.claim: estimated counterpart reservation is uncertain and can mislead targets
cons.example: treating a guessed reservation as fact

acceptance_tests: own reservation value derived from BATNA
ZOPA existence explicitly judged

nodes.definition: Expand the pie through integrative moves: logrolling across differently-valued issues, adding issues, and contingent agreements before dividing value.
contradictors: zero-sum bargainer who splits a fixed pie

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a new issue or differently-valued dimension is discovered

pros.claim: trading across issues each side values differently creates joint gains
pros.example: give flexible start date for a higher salary)

cons.claim: pushing value creation can leak information a hard counterpart exploits
cons.example: revealing low priority on an issue invites a grab

acceptance_tests: at least one logrolling trade identified
issues with asymmetric value listed

nodes.definition: Claim a fair share of the surplus through disciplined targets, justified offers, and protection against exploitation, after value is created.
contradictors: over-accommodator who never claims value

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the counterpart's claiming behavior or revealed reservation shifts

pros.claim: disciplined claiming captures a fair share without destroying the deal
pros.example: anchor with a justified number near your target)

cons.claim: aggressive claiming can sour the relationship and trigger impasse
cons.example: extreme demands that signal bad faith

acceptance_tests: target and limit set before claiming
every offer has a stated rationale

nodes.definition: Decide whether and how to open, set anchors with justification, and adjust against the counterpart's anchor without over-correcting.
contradictors: negotiator who always lets the other side open

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when information about the counterpart's reservation improves

pros.claim: a justified first offer anchors the bargaining range in your favor
pros.example: open with a market-backed number, not a round bluff)

cons.claim: a too-extreme anchor can insult and trigger impasse or counter-anchor war
cons.example: opening so high the other side walks

acceptance_tests: anchor has an explicit justification
adjustment stays tied to reservation value

nodes.definition: Plan concession magnitude, sequence, and labeling so each give is reciprocated and signals diminishing room toward the limit.
contradictors: unilateral conceder who gives without asking

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a concession is not reciprocated or the limit nears

pros.claim: trading concessions for reciprocal moves protects value and signals limits
pros.example: I can move on date if you move on price)

cons.claim: a predictable concession pattern lets the counterpart extract more
cons.example: equal steps invite one more demand

acceptance_tests: every concession is conditional on a reciprocal move
concession sizes shrink toward the limit

nodes.definition: Shape how options are perceived using gain/loss framing, reference points, and standards of fairness to make proposals more acceptable.
contradictors: plain-number negotiator who ignores presentation

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a fairness standard or reference point is contested

pros.claim: anchoring proposals to objective criteria depersonalizes disputes
pros.example: tie price to an independent index both accept)

cons.claim: manipulative framing that hides material facts is unethical and backfires
cons.example: framing a loss as a gain by omission

acceptance_tests: proposal tied to at least one objective standard
framing does not omit material facts

nodes.definition: Locate and grade the authority of negotiation and influence sources, separating evidence-based principles from folk tactics and pop heuristics.
contradictors: practitioner who cites a viral tactic as fact

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a cited influence claim lacks replication or a stronger source appears

pros.claim: grading sources stops weak pop-psych tactics from driving real decisions
pros.example: prefer replicated reciprocity research over a blog tip)

cons.claim: over-discounting practitioner wisdom can miss context-specific tactics
cons.example: rejecting all non-peer-reviewed advice

acceptance_tests: each principle graded by evidence strength
replication and context noted

nodes.definition: Apply and detect reciprocity: people return favors, concessions, and disclosures, including reject-then-retreat sequences.
contradictors: one-shot taker who never gives first

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when reciprocity is used coercively or a favor creates undue obligation

pros.claim: a genuine first concession often triggers a reciprocal move
pros.example: make a small real concession to unlock theirs)

cons.claim: exploitative reciprocity (unsolicited gifts) is manipulation and erodes trust
cons.example: a gift engineered only to create debt

acceptance_tests: reciprocal use stays within ethical limits
incoming obligation tactics flagged

nodes.definition: Use and audit social proof: people follow comparable others, especially under uncertainty and similarity.
contradictors: claimer of fake consensus

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when cited social proof is unrepresentative or fabricated

pros.claim: evidence that similar others chose X reduces uncertainty and resistance
pros.example: show peer companies that adopted the same terms)

cons.claim: fabricated or non-comparable social proof is deceptive and detectable
cons.example: fake reviews or cherry-picked peers

acceptance_tests: social proof comes from comparable, real cases
no fabricated consensus

nodes.definition: Use legitimate authority and expertise cues and resist illegitimate or manufactured authority pressure.
contradictors: title-dropper with irrelevant credentials

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when authority cues are irrelevant to the decision or manufactured

pros.claim: relevant, demonstrated expertise rightly increases persuasive weight
pros.example: cite a domain expert with a relevant track record)

cons.claim: appeals to irrelevant or fake authority are fallacies and manipulative
cons.example: a celebrity endorsing a technical claim

acceptance_tests: authority cited is relevant and real
irrelevant-authority pressure resisted

nodes.definition: Use genuine scarcity and deadlines truthfully and detect manufactured scarcity and false-urgency pressure.
contradictors: fabricator of fake deadlines

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a scarcity or deadline claim cannot be substantiated

pros.claim: truthful scarcity (real deadlines, limited supply) sharpens decisions
pros.example: a genuine expiring offer prompts timely choice)

cons.claim: manufactured scarcity is deceptive, illegal in some contexts, and erodes trust
cons.example: a fake 'today only' that recurs daily

acceptance_tests: every scarcity claim is factually substantiated
no fabricated deadlines

nodes.definition: Use voluntary, active, public commitments to build follow-through and resist low-ball and foot-in-the-door manipulation.
contradictors: coercer who manufactures false commitments

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a commitment is coerced or obtained by hidden low-ball

pros.claim: voluntary public commitments strongly predict follow-through
pros.example: have both sides restate agreed next steps in writing)

cons.claim: manufactured or coerced commitments break and damage trust
cons.example: low-balling then raising terms after a yes

acceptance_tests: commitments are voluntary and explicit
low-ball/foot-in-door tactics flagged

nodes.definition: Build genuine rapport, similarity, and goodwill to ease persuasion while guarding against ingratiation-based manipulation.
contradictors: flatterer who fakes similarity

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when rapport is feigned or used to mask a weak case

pros.claim: genuine rapport and shared ground lower defensiveness and unlock candor
pros.example: find a true common interest before hard issues)

cons.claim: manufactured liking and flattery are detectable and erode credibility
cons.example: scripted compliments that ring false

failure_modes: rapport used to mask weak case
acceptance_tests: rapport rests on genuine common ground
flattery-based manipulation avoided

nodes.definition: Use active listening, open questions, paraphrasing, and labeling to surface interests, reduce defensiveness, and verify understanding.
contradictors: interrupter who waits only to rebut

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when paraphrase reveals a misread interest or emotion

pros.claim: paraphrasing and labeling make the other side feel heard and reveal interests
pros.example: 'it sounds like timing matters most' invites confirmation)

cons.claim: performative listening without genuine adjustment backfires
cons.example: paraphrasing then ignoring what was said

acceptance_tests: key interests confirmed by paraphrase
open questions outnumber leading ones

nodes.definition: Structure high-stakes emotional conversations across the what-happened, feelings, and identity layers to move from blame to learning.
contradictors: blamer who frames it as one truth

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when identity or feelings stakes are higher than the substantive issue

pros.claim: separating what-happened, feelings, and identity defuses escalation
pros.example: name the feeling instead of arguing whose facts are right)

cons.claim: opening identity issues clumsily can deepen the rupture
cons.example: telling someone 'this is who you are' triggers defense

acceptance_tests: the three conversations separated explicitly
contribution framed jointly, not as blame

nodes.definition: Lower emotional intensity and reactive cycles using pacing, acknowledgment, reframing, and breaks so substantive talk can resume.
contradictors: escalator who matches heat with heat

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a reactive cycle or threat escalates beyond productive range

pros.claim: acknowledging emotion before content interrupts the reactive spiral
pros.example: 'I can see this is frustrating' before re-engaging substance)

cons.claim: premature reframing can feel dismissive and re-escalate
cons.example: rushing to solutions while someone still feels unheard

acceptance_tests: emotion acknowledged before content resumes
a break protocol exists for spikes

nodes.definition: Design and run a neutral third-party process that structures issues, manages caucuses, and guides parties to a self-determined agreement.
contradictors: arbiter who imposes a decision

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when impasse persists or a party loses trust in neutrality

pros.claim: a neutral process lets parties reach durable, self-owned agreements
pros.example: use caucuses to test reservation values privately)

cons.claim: perceived mediator bias collapses the process
cons.example: appearing to favor one side in joint session

acceptance_tests: process maintains visible neutrality
both parties' interests structured before solutions

nodes.definition: Distinguish ethical persuasion from manipulation and deception, set red lines, and detect dishonest tactics from the counterpart.
contradictors: win-at-all-costs tactician

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a planned or observed tactic crosses into deception or coercion

pros.claim: explicit red lines keep influence honest and legally safe
pros.example: ban fabricated facts and fake deadlines up front)

cons.claim: over-broad ethics rules can forbid legitimate framing and advocacy
cons.example: treating all framing as manipulation

acceptance_tests: red-line tactics enumerated and avoided
counterpart deception cues checked

nodes.definition: Convert agreement-in-principle into clear, committed, implementable terms with verification, contingencies, and relationship preservation.
contradictors: closer who leaves terms vague

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when terms are ambiguous or a side cannot actually deliver

pros.claim: clear, verified, contingent terms prevent post-deal disputes
pros.example: write who does what by when, with a dispute clause)

cons.claim: rushing closure leaves ambiguity that breaks the deal later
cons.example: a handshake with no written terms

acceptance_tests: every term is specific and verifiable
contingencies and dispute path defined

edges.why_related: the frame fixes which parties and issues the interest map must cover
edges.benefit_of_coupling: interests mapped to the right deal
edges.risk_of_conflict: mapping interests before framing maps the wrong deal
edges.example: map a hiring deal's interests only after scoping role+comp+start
edges.resolution_rule: fix the frame before mapping interests

edges.why_related: knowing interests lets you assess what alternatives actually satisfy them
edges.risk_of_conflict: BATNA built ignoring interests misvalues alternatives
edges.example: rate a job offer BATNA against your real priorities
edges.resolution_rule: establish interests before scoring alternatives

edges.why_related: reservation values are derived directly from each side's BATNA
edges.risk_of_conflict: reservation without BATNA is a guess
edges.example: set your floor from your second offer
edges.resolution_rule: compute BATNA before reservation value

edges.why_related: differently-weighted interests are the raw material for integrative trades
edges.risk_of_conflict: value creation without interest weights misses trades
edges.example: trade date flexibility for salary once weights are known
edges.resolution_rule: map interests before designing trades

edges.why_related: the ZOPA bounds the surplus that integrative moves expand
edges.benefit_of_coupling: creation aimed at a real surplus
edges.risk_of_conflict: expanding a non-existent pie wastes effort
edges.example: only logroll when a deal zone exists
edges.resolution_rule: confirm ZOPA before integrative design

edges.why_related: claiming targets and limits come from reservation values and the ZOPA
edges.risk_of_conflict: claiming with no reservation over- or under-shoots
edges.example: anchor inside the ZOPA, not beyond it
edges.resolution_rule: fix reservation/ZOPA before claiming

edges.why_related: expand the pie before dividing it so claiming does not foreclose joint gains
edges.risk_of_conflict: claiming first shrinks the pie
edges.example: explore trades before pushing on price
edges.resolution_rule: create value first, then claim, unless trust is too low

edges.why_related: the anchor is positioned relative to the ZOPA and target point
edges.risk_of_conflict: anchoring without ZOPA risks insult or leaving value
edges.example: open just outside their estimated reservation
edges.resolution_rule: set ZOPA before choosing the anchor

edges.why_related: the opening anchor sets the starting point the concession path moves from
edges.risk_of_conflict: conceding with no anchor loses the reference
edges.example: plan concessions down from your opening number
edges.resolution_rule: set the anchor before scheduling concessions

edges.why_related: framing chooses reference points and standards tied to mapped interests
edges.risk_of_conflict: framing without interests is empty spin
edges.example: frame a proposal around the interest they weight most
edges.resolution_rule: map interests before framing proposals

edges.why_related: the frame defines which influence claims and tactics are even relevant to grade
edges.risk_of_conflict: grading sources with no frame wastes effort
edges.example: evaluate tactics relevant to a B2B deal, not dating advice
edges.resolution_rule: frame the problem before grading sources

edges.why_related: applying reciprocity rests on graded evidence that the effect is real and context-fit
edges.risk_of_conflict: applying ungraded tactics propagates folk myths
edges.example: use replicated reciprocity research, not a viral clip
edges.resolution_rule: grade the source before applying the principle

edges.why_related: social proof use depends on graded evidence and comparable-case validity
edges.risk_of_conflict: ungraded proof spreads fake consensus
edges.example: cite vetted peer cases, not invented ones
edges.resolution_rule: grade sources before invoking social proof

edges.why_related: authority cues must be graded for relevance and legitimacy before use
edges.risk_of_conflict: ungraded authority invites the authority fallacy
edges.example: cite a relevant expert, not a famous name
edges.resolution_rule: grade authority relevance before citing it

edges.why_related: scarcity claims must be graded for truthfulness before use
edges.risk_of_conflict: ungraded scarcity becomes a fake deadline
edges.example: verify a deadline is real before invoking it
edges.resolution_rule: grade the scarcity claim before using it

edges.why_related: commitment tactics rest on graded evidence and must avoid coercive variants
edges.risk_of_conflict: ungraded use slides into low-balling
edges.example: use voluntary public commitments, not low-ball
edges.resolution_rule: grade evidence before engineering commitment

edges.why_related: active listening is the mechanism that surfaces and verifies mapped interests
edges.risk_of_conflict: mapping without listening fossilizes wrong guesses
edges.example: paraphrase to confirm what they actually want
edges.resolution_rule: use listening to validate the interest map

edges.why_related: the three-conversation method runs on active-listening and labeling skills
edges.risk_of_conflict: hard conversations without listening escalate
edges.example: label the feeling before debating facts
edges.resolution_rule: ground difficult conversations in active listening

edges.why_related: de-escalation uses acknowledgment and listening to interrupt reactive cycles
edges.risk_of_conflict: trying to de-escalate without listening reads as dismissive
edges.example: acknowledge frustration before re-engaging substance
edges.resolution_rule: use listening as the basis for de-escalation

edges.why_related: a mediator must first de-escalate before structuring issues
edges.risk_of_conflict: mediating a hot conflict without de-escalation fails
edges.example: cool the room before structuring issues
edges.resolution_rule: de-escalate before running the mediation process

edges.why_related: mediation structures each side's interests, so interest maps feed the process
edges.risk_of_conflict: mediating positions not interests deadlocks
edges.example: surface both sides' interests before proposing terms
edges.resolution_rule: map interests before structuring mediation

edges.why_related: ethics red lines are informed by which tactics are evidence-based vs deceptive
edges.risk_of_conflict: drawing ethics lines with no evidence is arbitrary
edges.example: ban tactics shown to be deceptive
edges.resolution_rule: grade tactics before drawing ethical red lines

edges.why_related: closure converts the claimed division into committed implementable terms
edges.risk_of_conflict: closing before claiming locks a bad split
edges.example: write final terms after the split is agreed
edges.resolution_rule: finalize claiming before drafting closure

edges.why_related: durable closure relies on voluntary, verified commitments
edges.risk_of_conflict: closing without real commitment yields broken deals
edges.example: have both sides restate commitments in writing
edges.resolution_rule: secure commitments before closing

edges.why_related: closure must respect ethics red lines and disclosure duties
edges.risk_of_conflict: closing on deceptive terms voids or breaks the deal
edges.example: disclose material facts before signing
edges.resolution_rule: clear ethics gate before closure

edges.why_related: BATNA strength bounds how aggressively you can credibly claim
edges.risk_of_conflict: claiming beyond BATNA leverage invites a walkout
edges.example: do not demand more than your alternative justifies
edges.resolution_rule: let BATNA bound the claiming target

edges.why_related: ethics red lines forbid manufactured scarcity and false deadlines
edges.risk_of_conflict: unbounded scarcity tactics become deception
edges.example: no fake 'today only' offers
edges.resolution_rule: ethics red lines override a tempting false-urgency tactic

edges.why_related: ethics bounds reciprocity to genuine concessions, not engineered debt
edges.risk_of_conflict: unbounded reciprocity becomes a manipulation
edges.example: no gift designed only to create obligation
edges.resolution_rule: ethics constrains how reciprocity may be used

edges.why_related: ethics bounds anchors to justifiable, non-deceptive numbers
edges.risk_of_conflict: deceptive anchors cross ethical lines
edges.example: anchor with a real basis, not a fabricated quote
edges.resolution_rule: ethics bounds the anchor's justification

edges.why_related: openness needed to create value conflicts with guardedness needed to claim it
edges.risk_of_conflict: too much openness leaks info; too much guarding kills joint gains
edges.example: revealing priorities to logroll invites a grab
edges.resolution_rule: create value first; switch to protected claiming once trades are mapped

edges.why_related: an aggressive anchor can damage rapport built for influence
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension between leverage and relationship made explicit
edges.risk_of_conflict: a hard anchor sours rapport; soft anchoring loses leverage
edges.example: a high opening offer chills a warm relationship
edges.resolution_rule: where relationship value is high, justify the anchor and soften delivery

edges.why_related: hard claiming pressures the goodwill that liking-based influence depends on
edges.risk_of_conflict: over-claiming burns rapport; over-preserving rapport under-claims
edges.example: pushing hard on price strains a long-term partner
edges.resolution_rule: preserve rapport when relationship value exceeds the marginal claim

edges.why_related: de-escalation may require conceding intensity that claiming wants to maintain
edges.risk_of_conflict: de-escalating can look like weakness; pressing can re-escalate
edges.example: backing off heat may invite a tougher demand
edges.resolution_rule: de-escalate first when the reactive cycle threatens the whole deal

edges.why_related: urgency pressure can undercut the warmth that liking-based persuasion builds
edges.risk_of_conflict: pushing urgency chills rapport; pure warmth loses momentum
edges.example: a hard deadline can feel coercive to a friendly counterpart
edges.resolution_rule: use truthful urgency sparingly when rapport is the main lever

edges.why_related: a stronger BATNA raises the credible aggressiveness of the opening anchor
edges.risk_of_conflict: a weak BATNA with a bold anchor gets called
edges.example: a firm second offer lets you open higher
edges.resolution_rule: let BATNA strength scale the anchor

edges.why_related: listening in dialogue can reveal interests that revise the original map
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignoring new signals fossilizes a stale map
edges.example: a paraphrase uncovers a hidden constraint
edges.resolution_rule: revise the interest map when listening surfaces new interests; stop when no new interests emerge in two exchanges

edges.why_related: a hard conversation can spike emotion and trigger a de-escalation loop
edges.risk_of_conflict: unmanaged spikes derail the conversation
edges.example: an identity threat flares and needs cooling
edges.resolution_rule: loop to de-escalation when emotion spikes; stop when intensity returns to workable range

edges.why_related: drafting terms can reveal a tactic that needs an ethics re-check
edges.risk_of_conflict: skipping the re-check signs a deceptive term
edges.example: a clause exposes an earlier nondisclosure
edges.resolution_rule: loop back to ethics when closure reveals a red-line issue; stop when terms pass the red-line checklist

edges.why_related: mediation can reveal the dispute was framed wrongly, forcing a reframe
edges.risk_of_conflict: mediating a misframed dispute wastes sessions
edges.example: caucuses reveal the real issue is trust, not price
edges.resolution_rule: reframe when mediation exposes a wrong frame; stop when both sides accept the reframed issues

edges.why_related: both are credibility heuristics people use under uncertainty
edges.risk_of_conflict: conflating them double-counts one cue
edges.example: peer adoption and expert endorsement both reduce doubt
edges.resolution_rule: treat as distinct cues; do not stack as if independent when they share a source

conflict_axes.trigger: openness needed to expand the pie versus guardedness needed to divide it
resolution_order: switch to disciplined claiming once trades are mapped
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: create value before claiming unless counterpart trust is too low to share information safely
conflict_axes.example: revealing low priority on an issue invites an immediate grab

conflict_axes.trigger: hard tactics needed for leverage erode the rapport that influence relies on
resolution_order: estimate relationship value vs marginal claim
if relationship dominates, soften delivery and justify asks
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: where future relationship value exceeds the marginal claim, the relationship dominates
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a long-term partner threatens to walk over an aggressive push
conflict_axes.example: pushing hard on price strains a strategic supplier

conflict_axes.trigger: lowering intensity to keep the talk alive can look like conceding leverage
resolution_order: judge whether the reactive cycle threatens the deal
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: de-escalation dominates when the reactive cycle threatens the whole negotiation
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: the counterpart is about to walk out in anger
conflict_axes.example: matching heat with heat ends the conversation

conflict_axes.trigger: a deceptive tactic would work in the short term but crosses an ethical or legal line
resolution_order: check the tactic against red lines
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: ethics red lines dominate; deceptive tactics are forbidden regardless of short-term payoff
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a fabricated deadline or fake authority would close the deal
conflict_axes.example: a fake 'final offer' that is not final

conflict_axes.trigger: pressure to close fast versus the rework risk of unprepared terms
resolution_order: require BATNA/ZOPA before any irreversible commitment
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: preparation dominates before irreversible commitments; speed yields to a grounded walk-away
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a same-day signature is demanded with no BATNA

conflict_axes.trigger: framing to make a proposal acceptable risks omitting material facts
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: disclosure of material facts dominates; framing may shape emphasis but not hide facts
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a gain-frame omits a material downside
conflict_axes.example: presenting only upside while hiding a known risk

conflict_axes.trigger: conceding to build momentum versus holding firm to protect value
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: reciprocity-conditioned concessions dominate; never concede without a reciprocal move near the limit
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: the counterpart pockets concessions without moving
conflict_axes.example: equal unilateral concessions invite one more demand

conflict_axes.trigger: stacking authority and social proof that share a source double-counts one cue
resolution_order: do not present correlated cues as independent
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: independence check dominates; correlated cues are not stacked as if independent
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: the same body endorses and is cited as peer adoption
conflict_axes.example: expert and 'everyone' both trace to one promoter

conflict_axes.trigger: a mediator's drive to settle can compromise visible neutrality
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: neutrality dominates; the mediator structures process but parties own the settlement
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a party perceives the mediator favors the other side
conflict_axes.example: steering toward a settlement the mediator prefers

edge_cases.trigger: a viral or pop-psych tactic is applied as if evidence-based
edge_cases.example: treating a single blog claim about a tactic as established
edge_cases.detection_method: check each applied principle against the graded source list and replication status
resolution: downgrade the tactic to heuristic
require a graded source before reuse

edge_cases.trigger: a bluffed or non-existent alternative is treated as real leverage
edge_cases.failure_mode: claiming beyond real leverage triggers a walkout
edge_cases.example: citing an imaginary competing offer that gets called
edge_cases.detection_method: require the BATNA to name a concrete, currently available option
resolution: replace bluff with a real alternative or lower the claim
re-derive reservation value

edge_cases.trigger: a deadline or supply limit is fabricated to pressure
edge_cases.failure_mode: deception that voids trust and may be illegal
edge_cases.example: a 'today only' price that recurs every day
edge_cases.detection_method: verify every scarcity claim against a real constraint before use
resolution: remove the fabricated claim
substitute a truthful constraint or drop the tactic

edge_cases.trigger: a deceptive tactic is rationalized as mere framing
edge_cases.failure_mode: ethical red line crossed under cover of persuasion
edge_cases.example: omitting a material defect and calling it positive framing
edge_cases.detection_method: run the tactic through the red-line checklist and material-disclosure test
resolution: disclose the material fact
reject the tactic and log a decision record

edge_cases.trigger: the negotiation is treated as zero-sum and integrative trades are skipped
edge_cases.failure_mode: joint value left on the table
edge_cases.example: splitting price when a date-for-price trade would help both
edge_cases.detection_method: test whether any two issues are valued differently by the two sides
resolution: run a logrolling search before claiming
add issues to widen the deal

edge_cases.trigger: an extreme anchor insults the counterpart and triggers impasse
edge_cases.failure_mode: relationship and deal damaged by the opening
edge_cases.example: opening so high the other side walks out
edge_cases.detection_method: compare the anchor to the estimated reservation and relationship value
resolution: re-anchor with justification
soften delivery while keeping the number defensible

edge_cases.trigger: concessions are given without securing reciprocal moves
edge_cases.failure_mode: value bled away with no return
edge_cases.example: lowering price three times while they hold firm
edge_cases.detection_method: check that every concession is conditioned on a reciprocal move
resolution: stop unconditional concessions
re-tie each give to a specific ask

edge_cases.trigger: emotion escalates into a reactive cycle that derails substance
edge_cases.failure_mode: talks break down before issues are addressed
edge_cases.example: both sides trading accusations instead of interests
edge_cases.detection_method: monitor for rising intensity and matched-heat exchanges
resolution: acknowledge emotion and pause
loop to de-escalation before resuming substance

edge_cases.trigger: the mediator is perceived as favoring one side
edge_cases.failure_mode: process collapses as trust in neutrality fails
edge_cases.example: appearing to push one party's preferred terms in joint session
edge_cases.detection_method: audit process moves for symmetric treatment of both parties
resolution: restate neutrality and process rules
re-balance airtime and caucus access

edge_cases.trigger: agreement is closed with ambiguous, unverified terms
edge_cases.detection_method: test each term for specificity, ownership, and a verification method
resolution: rewrite terms to be specific and verifiable
add a dispute mechanism and implementation plan

edge_cases.trigger: the create-vs-claim tension is encoded as a dependency instead of a conflict
edge_cases.failure_mode: sequencing logic hides a real tradeoff
edge_cases.example: treating claiming as merely 'after' creation with no tension
edge_cases.detection_method: verify create-claim is modeled as both a sequence and a separate conflict edge/axis
resolution: separate the dependency from the conflict
ensure the conflict axis carries the tradeoff

workflow.objective: fix the negotiation frame and success criteria
acceptance_tests: frame names parties, issues, horizon, criteria
workflow.do_first_because: the frame is the highest-coupling foundation every later step inherits

workflow.objective: map interests behind positions and verify them by listening
acceptance_tests: every position traced to an interest
workflow.do_first_because: interests are the raw material for both alternatives and trades

workflow.objective: ground leverage in BATNAs, reservation values, and the ZOPA
acceptance_tests: own BATNA is a concrete available option
ZOPA existence judged
workflow.do_first_because: a grounded walk-away must precede any tactic or commitment

workflow.objective: design integrative trades, then a disciplined claiming plan
acceptance_tests: at least one logrolling trade found
target and limit set
workflow.do_first_because: expanding value before dividing it prevents foreclosing joint gains

workflow.objective: grade influence sources and set ethics red lines before deploying tactics
acceptance_tests: each principle graded by evidence
red-line tactics enumerated
workflow.do_first_because: tactics must be evidence-graded and ethics-bounded before they are used

workflow.objective: select and bound the persuasion principles that fit the audience and context
acceptance_tests: each principle's use within ethical limits
detection checklist present
workflow.do_first_because: principles must be chosen on graded evidence and within red lines

workflow.objective: sequence anchoring, concessions, and framing from the ZOPA
acceptance_tests: anchor has explicit justification
every concession conditioned on a reciprocal move
workflow.do_first_because: tactics depend on a fixed ZOPA and bounded principles

workflow.objective: run the conversation, managing emotion and reactive cycles
acceptance_tests: emotion acknowledged before content when it spikes
workflow.do_first_because: high-stakes talks fail without active emotion and reactive-cycle management

workflow.objective: if impasse persists, run a neutral third-party process
acceptance_tests: process maintains visible neutrality
workflow.do_first_because: a neutral process is the fallback when direct talks deadlock

workflow.objective: convert agreement into clear, committed, implementable, ethics-cleared terms
acceptance_tests: every term specific and verifiable
red-line checklist passed
workflow.do_first_because: closure must not be hard-locked before terms, ethics, and human review pass

priority_rationale.notes: verifies interests live, feeds conflict skills
grades tactics before they are used
red lines gate tactics and closure
durable terms; closed last, reviewed before lock

dominance_rules.trigger: an irreversible or high-risk commitment is requested before validation completes
dominance_rules.rule: high-risk or irreversible commitments require validation proportional to irreversibility before lock
dominance_rules.required_action: block AGREEMENT_CLOSURE hard lock until human review and acceptance tests pass
dominance_rules.example: refuse to sign a major commitment with no BATNA on a same-day deadline

dominance_rules.trigger: a deceptive tactic would be effective in the short term
dominance_rules.rule: ethics red lines override short-term effectiveness; deceptive tactics are forbidden
dominance_rules.required_action: reject the tactic and substitute an honest alternative; log a decision record
dominance_rules.example: drop a fabricated 'final offer' even though it would close the deal

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-value tactic is ready before its prerequisite analysis is complete
dominance_rules.required_action: complete BATNA/ZOPA before anchoring or claiming
dominance_rules.example: do not anchor before the ZOPA is established

dominance_rules.trigger: a precise tactic rests on an ungraded or folk source
dominance_rules.rule: evidence label and source grading override numeric precision
dominance_rules.required_action: downgrade ungraded tactics to heuristic and require a graded source
dominance_rules.example: prefer a replicated reciprocity finding over a confidently-stated blog tip

dominance_rules.trigger: a node is proposed for lock before its acceptance tests pass
dominance_rules.rule: acceptance tests and validation override the urge to lock
dominance_rules.required_action: keep the node in draft/soft_lock until tests pass
dominance_rules.example: do not lock the closure terms before the clarity gate passes

dominance_rules.trigger: a node has risk_if_wrong>=0.80 or an irreversible commitment is at stake
dominance_rules.rule: human review overrides automated progression for high-risk or irreversible steps
dominance_rules.required_action: route the step to a human reviewer before finalization
dominance_rules.example: a major commitment closure requires human sign-off

dominance_rules.trigger: marginal claiming would damage a relationship whose future value exceeds the gain
dominance_rules.rule: when future relationship value exceeds the marginal claim, preserve the relationship
dominance_rules.required_action: soften delivery and forgo the marginal claim; justify any firm ask
dominance_rules.example: ease off a small price push with a long-term strategic partner

dominance_rules.trigger: a reactive cycle threatens to end the negotiation
dominance_rules.rule: de-escalation overrides pressing advantage when the reactive cycle threatens the deal
dominance_rules.required_action: acknowledge emotion and pause before resuming substance
dominance_rules.example: stop pushing and cool the room when the counterpart is about to walk

dominance_rules.trigger: claiming starts before integrative trades are explored
dominance_rules.rule: value creation precedes claiming unless trust is too low to share information
dominance_rules.required_action: run a logrolling search before switching to protected claiming
dominance_rules.example: explore date-for-price trades before pushing hard on price

dominance_rules.trigger: persuasive framing would omit a material fact
dominance_rules.rule: disclosure of material facts overrides persuasive framing
dominance_rules.required_action: disclose the material fact; framing may shape emphasis but not hide facts
dominance_rules.example: reveal a known material downside even when a gain-frame would land better

anti_rework_rules.rule: fix the negotiation frame before any interest mapping or tactic
anti_rework_rules.rationale: tactics run against the wrong frame are pure rework
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: anchoring or claiming begins before the frame is set
anti_rework_rules.example: haggling price before scoping the real deal

anti_rework_rules.rule: map interests before designing integrative trades or claiming
anti_rework_rules.rationale: trades built on guessed interests are redone when real interests surface
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: logrolling proposed with no interest weights
anti_rework_rules.example: trading an issue you wrongly assumed they value

anti_rework_rules.rule: establish BATNA, reservation, and ZOPA before anchoring, claiming, or closing
anti_rework_rules.rationale: tactics with no grounded walk-away over- or under-shoot
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: an anchor or commitment is set with no reservation value
anti_rework_rules.example: opening a number before knowing your floor

anti_rework_rules.rule: grade influence sources before applying any persuasion principle
anti_rework_rules.rationale: ungraded tactics propagate folk myths and may be unethical
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a principle is applied before its source is graded
anti_rework_rules.example: using a viral tactic as if it were established

anti_rework_rules.rule: set ethics red lines before selecting and deploying tactics
anti_rework_rules.rationale: deploying tactics with no red lines invites manipulation and legal risk
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: tactics are deployed before red lines exist
anti_rework_rules.example: using a fake deadline because no red line forbade it

anti_rework_rules.rule: explore integrative value before switching to claiming
anti_rework_rules.rationale: claiming first shrinks the pie and forecloses joint gains
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: claiming starts with no logrolling search
anti_rework_rules.example: splitting price before any date-for-price trade

anti_rework_rules.rule: set the anchor before scheduling concessions
anti_rework_rules.rationale: concessions with no anchor lose the reference and bleed value
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: concessions planned with no opening number
anti_rework_rules.example: conceding from an undefined starting point

anti_rework_rules.rule: de-escalate before resuming substance when emotion spikes
anti_rework_rules.rationale: pushing substance during a reactive spiral derails and redoes the conversation
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: substance pressed while intensity is high
anti_rework_rules.example: arguing facts while someone still feels unheard

anti_rework_rules.rule: complete human review before any irreversible commitment
anti_rework_rules.rationale: irreversible moves made before review cannot be undone
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a high-risk closure is finalized with no review
anti_rework_rules.example: signing a major commitment with no sign-off

anti_rework_rules.rule: pass acceptance tests and traceability before any hard lock
anti_rework_rules.rationale: hard-locking before tests yields a defective, hard-to-change agreement
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a hard lock is requested before tests pass
anti_rework_rules.example: locking terms before the clarity gate passes

iteration_protocol.trigger: validator or negotiation review reports a failure
acceptance_tests: every failure mapped to a subsystem

iteration_protocol.detection: rank by risk and downstream coupling
acceptance_tests: high-risk defects ranked first

iteration_protocol.trigger: a fix may affect dependent nodes or locked items
iteration_protocol.detection: trace dependents of the changed item
acceptance_tests: all dependents of the change identified

iteration_protocol.trigger: a defect is routed to the wrong subsystem
action: route each defect to its owner subsystem
acceptance_tests: each defect handled by its routed owner
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: all queued defects routed and repaired

iteration_protocol.trigger: a repair changed a locked or high-coupling component
iteration_protocol.detection: re-run the validator after each batch
acceptance_tests: no new failures introduced

iteration_protocol.trigger: new evidence changes a node's importance beyond the revisit delta
action: update priority if delta exceeds threshold
acceptance_tests: posterior recomputed from current evidence

iteration_protocol.trigger: a high-risk or irreversible defect cannot be auto-repaired
iteration_protocol.detection: detect risk_if_wrong>=0.80 or irreversible flag on an unresolved defect
action: package the issue for human review
acceptance_tests: human reviewer assigned

iteration_protocol.trigger: remaining defects are low-risk and below materiality
iteration_protocol.detection: count unresolved low-risk defects against tolerance
acceptance_tests: no high-risk or irreversible defects open
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: no material defects remain or max iterations reached

human_review_required_for: irreversible commitments equivalent to market entry or major deals
claiming a position without a real BATNA
deploying a tactic that nears an ethics red line
hard lock of the final agreement

recomputed all derived fields from base estimates via formula script
